page: Microsoft Azure DC8as_v5 is a general-purpose instance powered by the AMD EPYC 9V74 processor built on the x86_64 architecture. The instance allocates 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Memory capacity stands at 32 GB, providing a standard 4 GB per vCPU ratio, backed by 32 MB of L3 cache and 1 MB of L2 cache per core. It lacks integrated GPUs and includes no local ephemeral storage, meaning disk operations rely completely on attached network storage such as Azure Premium SSDs.

In synthetic benchmark evaluations, the DC8as_v5 demonstrates consistent middle-tier performance relative to other instances in its resource class. The processor features standard vector and security capabilities including AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, while omitting AVX-512 and AMX instructions. Compute benchmarks reveal a stress-ng single-core score of 2,330.38 and a multi-core score of 9,289.94, alongside a Geekbench single-core result of 1,439.0 and multi-core score of 5,485.0. Memory throughput and execution efficiency remain stable, yielding a PassMark CPU score of 10,755.64, a memory score of 2,125.08, and Redis throughput reaching 8.0 million operations per second.

Given its balanced compute-to-memory profile and middle-of-the-pack benchmark baseline, the instance delivers dependable efficiency for routine enterprise services. The absence of local disk requires external volume planning, introducing a potential storage latency tradeoff depending on network storage tiering. As a result, the DC8as_v5 is suitable for web serving tiers, software compilation tasks, intermediate caching nodes, microservices hosting, and general relational database operations where specialized high-vector processing is unnecessary.
description: Microsoft Azure DC8as_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture and powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. The instance provides 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores alongside 32 GB of system memory, matching a balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio. It lacks integrated local storage, requiring attached persistent disks for all file operations, and does not include GPU acceleration. Hardware capabilities include cryptographic extensions such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, though AVX-512 is not supported. Synthetic benchmark results place the system in the middle tier of its peer group, highlighted by a PassMark CPU rating of 10,755.64, Geekbench multi-core score of 5,485.0, and Redis throughput of 8.0 million operations per second. The instance provides steady resource allocation well suited for application hosting, CI/CD compilation, enterprise microservices, and general database workloads.
